'''Leslie Morgan Smith''' (born August 15, 1961){{r|cv}} is an American applied mathematician, mechanical engineer, and engineering physicist whose research focuses on [[fluid dynamics]] and [[turbulence]]. She is a professor of mathematics and of engineering physics at the [[University of Wisconsin]].

==Education==
Smith graduated ''[[Latin honors|cum laude]]'' with a bachelor's degree in physics from [[Harvard University]] in 1983.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. in applied mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1988. Her dissertation, ''An upper bound with correct scaling laws for turbulent shear flows'', was supervised by [[Willem Malkus]].{{r|cv|mg}}

== Career ==
After postdoctoral research at [[Stanford University]], the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]], and [[Princeton University]], she became an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at [[Yale University]] in 1993, and moved to the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1998,{{r|cv}} jointly affiliated with the departments of mathematics and mechanical engineering. In 2002 she was promoted to full professor, and moved from mechanical engineering to engineering physics.{{r|promo}} She served as chair of mathematics from 2005 to 2008, and again 2012 to 2014,{{r|cv}} becoming the first female chair of the department.{{r|strength}}

==Recognition==
Smith was named a [[List of American Physical Society Fellows (1998–2010)|Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2008 "for important and insightful contributions to the understanding of turbulence in engineering and geophysical flows through theory and numerical simulations".{{r|faps}} She was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], in the 2022 class of fellows, "for contributions to applied mathematics and particularly fluid mechanics".{{r|fams}}
